result.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
result.summary: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ToRA：把第二个模型作为生成器解码步中的「额外一行」，共享权重与 KV cache，用双行 kernel 一次性读取权重，实现低开销的流式安全检测，在 Qwen3-0.6B 上以不到 4% 的每 token 延迟超过专用 guard 与 hidden-state probe。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以极小增量算力在读隐藏状态上做逐 token 判定」的工程路径，可能为 LVR 中的低开销验证头或 STOP 决策提供借鉴，但属纯文本安全场景，迁移需核查。
